trigger: teardown_claimed never calls unpin() or checks final_written before erasing a record
summary: Distinct from CS-2: a record parked kRingOnly by the stale-arm backstop, then claimed and torn down by a LATER sweep pass (session-death or pin-acked reasons) BEFORE the still-ticking pump calls on_final_written, is erased entirely - find_locked then returns null, on_final_written returns false, and since teardown_claimed never calls unpin(), the pin leaks permanently rather than being credited by UP-1's widened accept path. Verified this round that teardown_claimed contains no unpin/final_written reference at all (grepped the full function body). NOT fixed this round: the reporting agent rated this 'likely, not verified' and explicitly flagged an unresolved precondition (whether the session's pin bookkeeping outlives the erased BridgeRecord) that could bound or moot the leak; closing it properly needs either an unpin sweep in teardown_claimed's kNone path or a stricter no-claim-while-pump-may-still-write guard, neither of which is a small fix. Recorded honestly as found-but-not-closed rather than either patched hastily or left unrecorded.
waiver_rationale: Non-gating (derived MEDIUM/SHOULD). Filed as https://github.com/Tr3kkR/Yuzu/issues/2780 (2026-08-04), dedupe-checked against #2739/#2740 (both related, both distinct root causes).

trigger: sweep Pass 3's victim-selection loop re-scans the full records_ map, taking every record's own lock, once per victim visited
summary: Found by Doomgoose (PR #2781 external review, collaborator). O(records x victims) mutex traffic where the pass's own comment claims O(records)/microseconds - traced to a4809554 in this branch's own history (not present on origin/dev), and NOT gated by --mcp-enable-streamed-post since this pass already serves the pre-existing GET-only bridge. A plan to fix it by removing the per-victim cap check was reviewed by a Fable-backed architect BEFORE implementation and found (by reasoning about the loop shape, not a measured multiplier) to risk over-expiry of client-recoverable parked state with no bound on how far past the target it could run; the plan was revised to a pass-local live counter (decremented only for teardowns this pass commits) that preserves the exact down-to-cap stopping point at O(1) per visit instead of O(records). Fixed: one entry scan builds a parked_seq-sorted candidate list; the pass-local counter gates the visiting loop; a single fresh rescan at the end (not per-victim) re-tests the cap for mark-clearing and the exhausted-budget counter, per the same #2489 freshness requirement the original code already established. Mutation-verified with a new test (6 claimable parked records across 2 sessions, cap 2): removing the live>cap bound turns record_count()==2 into 0 and forced_expire count 4 into 6. Wave-4 governance re-review (consistency-auditor) flagged the original "up to 3x" figure as an unanchored number presented at epistemic_status=verified; corrected here to a qualitative claim, since only the fix + the mutation test (not a specific multiplier) were independently verified.

trigger: on_final_written_() called with no exception containment immediately after the final frame's write_all() already succeeded
summary: Found by Doomgoose (PR #2781 external review). If on_final_written_ throws (a modelled fault class elsewhere in this file pair - mutex lock failure), pump_once's outer catch stamped kInternalError even though the client already received a correct, complete result - misreporting a successful call as an internal fault - while the bridge's credit step (final_written + unpin) never ran, silently retaining the session's pin. Third occurrence of this leak-on-credit-failure shape (CS-1/CS-2/UP-1), this time via an uncontained exception rather than a race. Fixed: the call is now contained; on failure, note_close_reason(kCompleted) runs FIRST (first-wins beats a later kInternalError from a fault in the log/counter themselves - a real ordering bug in the first drafted fix, caught by the Fable plan review before implementation), then a new dedicated counter (yuzu_mcp_stream_final_credit_failed_total, matching the existing yuzu_mcp_bridge_charge_release_deferred_total precedent) plus a log line run in their own nested guard. kCompleted confirmed as the right close reason (not a new one) since the client-observable fact is identical to the ordinary success path and a distinct close reason would require a second, structurally-forbidden terminal frame. Mutation-verified: removing the try/catch turns close_reason()==kCompleted into kInternalError and the new counter stays at 0 instead of 1. Wave-4 governance re-review (consistency-auditor) flagged the original line citation (1514) as the on_final_written_ guard, not the try block; corrected to 1524.

trigger: the down-to-cap pressure test uses an all-claimable population, so live (decremented only on a committed teardown) and visit_budget (decremented on every visit) move in lockstep and no test exercises them diverging
summary: Independently found by quality-engineer and unhappy-path (UP-3) in the same wave-4 review: a defer-heavy population never decrements live, so the loop drains the full candidate list without live ever satisfying the cap - the exact shape pressure_budget_exhausted exists to surface, and it was untested. Fixed: added a new TEST_CASE ("deferred victims consume visit budget without decrementing live...") using the existing park_deferring_a_and_claimable_b fault-injection technique (persistent visitor copy-OOM) extended to 3 deferring + 2 claimable records across 2 sessions, cap 1 - parked (and therefore visited, oldest-first) with ALL 3 defers before BOTH claims, the ordering that makes a live-miscounting bug externally observable via record_count/phase_for rather than silently absorbed by defers that stay parked either way. Verified (first draft, interleaved defer/claim/defer/claim/defer order): traced by hand that an early-exit bug would not change the observable result in that ordering, so it was reordered before relying on it as evidence. Mutation-verified on the reordered version: injected an unconditional --live decrement statement after every visit (server/core/src/mcp_stream_bridge.cpp, right after the stage-2 atomic visit, reverted after the check) - 4 of 5 pressure tests in the file went red, including this one at exactly the predicted symptom (record_count 4 vs expected 3, the second claimable record left in kRingOnly instead of reaped, forced_expire{synthesize_unavailable} 1.0 vs expected 2.0). Reverted; full [2489] tag group (233 assertions, 5 test cases) green afterward.
